name: Craft
description: Craft is a collaborative writing and knowledge workspace for documents, linked pages, daily notes, tasks, folders, and structured collections. Individuals and teams use its native apps and web editor to capture ideas, organize projects, publish polished documents, and keep shared knowledge connected.
agentUseSummary: Connect Relay to Craft's official hosted MCP server with OAuth, select one Craft space, then let agents use its live read or management tools under Safe or Dangerous policy.

credentialRequirements.name: CRAFT_API_URL
credentialRequirements.label: Craft API connection URL
credentialRequirements.helpText: Compatibility only: existing Craft API connection URLs remain supported. New connections use Craft's official hosted MCP OAuth flow.

capabilities.label: Read workspace knowledge
capabilities.description: Use provider-declared read-only MCP tools for the Craft space selected during authorization.

capabilities.label: Manage workspace knowledge
capabilities.description: Use provider-declared MCP mutations in the Craft space selected during authorization.

allowed.label: Read Craft content
allowed.description: Use one live-schema-verified read tool from Craft's official hosted MCP server.

approvalRequired.label: Manage Craft content
approvalRequired.description: Use one live-schema-verified mutation from Craft's official hosted MCP server; Safe mode requires approval.

blocked.label: Mount raw Craft MCP
blocked.description: Relay separates provider-declared read-only tools from mutations and does not expose an ungoverned MCP surface.

blocked.label: Expose Craft credentials
blocked.description: OAuth tokens and legacy API connection URLs remain encrypted and never enter tool inputs, results, logs, or audits.

blocked.label: Transfer unbounded content
blocked.description: Requests, responses, arrays, nesting, and query fields remain inside Relay bounds.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Provider-declared read-only MCP tools run directly; every Craft mutation requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected connection-authorized Craft operation runs without Relay per-action approval; exact authority, provider permissions, operation allowlists, bounds, redaction, audits, and fair-use limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway connects to Craft's official hosted MCP server and mounts bounded read and manage wrappers without exposing OAuth credentials.
Railway connects to Craft's official hosted MCP server and mounts bounded read and manage wrappers without exposing OAuth credentials.

providerSetup.blocker: No signed-in Craft account was available for live OAuth consent and authenticated MCP tools/list verification.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer connects Craft in Relay, selects one space in Craft's OAuth consent, then verifies live tool discovery, bounded reads, Safe mutation approval, Dangerous mutation, refresh, revocation, and disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Craft's current official client guide publishes the shared https://mcp.craft.do/my/mcp endpoint, Streamable HTTP transport, browser authorization, and one-space selection.
Craft's live OAuth metadata publishes authorization, token, dynamic registration, and revocation endpoints with S256 PKCE and refresh-token support.

Craft documents customer-created API Connections with selected document or full-space authority, configurable access permissions, secret endpoint credentials, search, daily-note and task access, document mutations, collections, and advanced filters.
Craft's official Space API reference documents the stable blocks, search, collections, documents, folders, and tasks read and mutation endpoints used by Relay's operation allowlists.
Craft documents space-bound connections, cryptographically unguessable links, independently selected read/write permissions, content-scope restrictions, rotation, and least-privilege guidance.

Craft describes its product integration surface across documents, daily notes, tasks, collections, API automation, MCP, native Apple automation, and deep links, with API and MCP usage included under fair-use limits.
